title: Vote share cutoff and policy adoption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the 50% vote-share cutoff. The treatment (policy adoption) turns on deterministically when running_var ≥ 0.5.
- Why: Treatment status is a known, deterministic function of the running variable at a known cutoff. The RDD identifies the causal jump in outcomes at the threshold.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff: In the absence of treatment, E[y0 | running_var = c−] = E[y0 | running_var = c+].
  - No precise manipulation of the running variable around 0.5 (density smoothness).
  - Correct specification of the local approximation near the cutoff (we use local linear with triangular kernel and robust bias-correction; we probe robustness to bandwidths, polynomial order, kernels, and donuts).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load or install required packages
req_pkgs <- c("rdrobust", "rddensity", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in req_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(rdrobust)
  library(rddensity)
  library(sandwich)
  library(lmtest)
})

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s25_data.csv")

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("running_var","treated","y","near_cutoff") %in% names(df)))
x <- df$running_var
y <- df$y
cut <- 0.5

# Helper to extract robust bias-corrected (BC) estimate, SE, and p-value from rdrobust object
extract_rd <- function(res) {
  # Try multiple object structures for robustness across versions
  out <- list(tau = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
  # Newer versions: res$coef, res$se, res$pv with names
  if (!is.null(res$coef)) {
    nm <- names(res$coef)
    if (!is.null(nm) && any(grepl("bc", nm, ignore.case=TRUE))) {
      out$tau <- as.numeric(res$coef[grep("bc", nm, ignore.case=TRUE)[1]])
    } else {
      out$tau <- as.numeric(res$coef[min(2, length(res$coef))])
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(res$se)) {
    nm <- names(res$se)
    if (!is.null(nm) && any(grepl("rb|rob", nm, ignore.case=TRUE))) {
      out$se <- as.numeric(res$se[grep("rb|rob", nm, ignore.case=TRUE)[1]])
    } else {
      out$se <- as.numeric(res$se[min(2, length(res$se))])
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(res$pv)) {
    nm <- names(res$pv)
    if (!is.null(nm) && any(grepl("rb|rob", nm, ignore.case=TRUE))) {
      out$p <- as.numeric(res$pv[grep("rb|rob", nm, ignore.case=TRUE)[1]])
    } else {
      out$p <- as.numeric(res$pv[min(2, length(res$pv))])
    }
  }
  # Fallback for older versions with Estimate matrix
  if ((is.na(out$tau) || is.na(out$se) || is.na(out$p)) && !is.null(res$Estimate)) {
    est_mat <- res$Estimate
    rn <- rownames(est_mat)
    # Prefer Bias-Corrected row if available
    idx <- if (!is.null(rn) && any(grepl("Bias", rn))) {
      grep("Bias", rn)[1]
    } else {
      1
    }
    # Try common column names
    coef_col <- if ("Coef." %in% colnames(est_mat)) "Coef." else if ("coef" %in% colnames(est_mat)) "coef" else colnames(est_mat)[1]
    se_col   <- if ("Std. Err." %in% colnames(est_mat)) "Std. Err." else if ("se" %in% colnames(est_mat)) "se" else colnames(est_mat)[2]
    pv_col   <- if ("P>|z|" %in% colnames(est_mat)) "P>|z|" else if ("pval" %in% colnames(est_mat)) "pval" else tail(colnames(est_mat), 1)
    out$tau <- if (is.na(out$tau)) as.numeric(est_mat[idx, coef_col]) else out$tau
    out$se  <- if (is.na(out$se))  as.numeric(est_mat[idx, se_col])  else out$se
    out$p   <- if (is.na(out$p))   as.numeric(est_mat[idx, pv_col])  else out$p
  }
  out
}

# Function to run rdrobust with options and print a concise line
run_rd <- function(x, y, c = 0.5, p = 1, kernel = "triangular", h = NULL, sample_idx = NULL, label = "RD") {
  if (is.null(sample_idx)) sample_idx <- rep(TRUE, length(x))
  h_arg <- if (is.null(h)) NULL else c(h, h)
  res <- rdrobust(y[sample_idx], x[sample_idx], c = c, p = p, kernel = kernel, h = h_arg)
  est <- extract_rd(res)
  pct <- 100 * (exp(est$tau) - 1)
  cat(sprintf("%s: tau_BC = %.4f, SE_rob = %.4f, p = %.4f, implied %% change = %.2f%%\n",
              label, est$tau, est$se, est$p, pct))
  invisible(list(res = res, est = est))
}

cat("=== Main RDD estimate (local linear, triangular kernel, MSE-optimal bandwidth, within |x-0.5|<=0.3) ===\n")
samp_main <- df$near_cutoff == 1
main_fit <- run_rd(x, y, c = cut, p = 1, kernel = "triangular", h = NULL, sample_idx = samp_main, 
                   label = "Main RD")

# Density (manipulation) test at the cutoff
cat("\n=== McCrary density test at cutoff ===\n")
dens <- rddensity(x, c = cut)
print(summary(dens))

# Robustness: alternative bandwidths
cat("\n=== Robustness: Alternative bandwidths (local linear, triangular) ===\n")
for (h in c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20)) {
  run_rd(x, y, c = cut, p = 1, kernel = "triangular", h = h, sample_idx = samp_main,
         label = paste0("h = ", h))
}

# Robustness: quadratic local polynomial
cat("\n=== Robustness: Local quadratic (p=2), triangular kernel ===\n")
run_rd(x, y, c = cut, p = 2, kernel = "triangular", h = NULL, sample_idx = samp_main, 
       label = "Local quadratic")

# Robustness: uniform kernel
cat("\n=== Robustness: Local linear with uniform kernel ===\n")
run_rd(x, y, c = cut, p = 1, kernel = "uniform", h = NULL, sample_idx = samp_main, 
       label = "Uniform kernel")

# Robustness: donut hole (exclude very near-cutoff obs)
cat("\n=== Robustness: Donut RD excluding |x-0.5| < 0.01 ===\n")
donut <- samp_main & (abs(x - cut) >= 0.01)
run_rd(x, y, c = cut, p = 1, kernel = "triangular", h = NULL, sample_idx = donut, 
       label = "Donut 0.01")

# Placebo cutoffs (should be near zero)
cat("\n=== Placebo cutoffs (should show no significant jump) ===\n")
run_rd(x, y, c = 0.45, p = 1, kernel = "triangular", h = NULL, sample_idx = samp_main, 
       label = "Placebo c=0.45")
run_rd(x, y, c = 0.55, p = 1, kernel = "triangular", h = NULL, sample_idx = samp_main, 
       label = "Placebo c=0.55")

# Global polynomial RD within ±0.3 (flexible slopes on both sides)
cat("\n=== Robustness: Global cubic polynomial with side-specific slopes (within ±0.3) ===\n")
dist <- x - cut
samp_poly <- abs(dist) <= 0.3
mod <- lm(y ~ treated + dist + I(dist^2) + I(dist^3) +
            treated:dist + treated:I(dist^2) + treated:I(dist^3),
          data = df, subset = samp_poly)
vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(mod, type = "HC2")
ct <- coeftest(mod, vcov = vc)
tau_g <- coef(mod)["treated"]
se_g <- sqrt(diag(vc))["treated"]
p_g <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(tau_g / se_g)))
pct_g <- 100 * (exp(tau_g) - 1)
cat(sprintf("Global poly RD (cubic): tau = %.4f, SE_HC2 = %.4f, p = %.4f, implied %% change = %.2f%%\n",
            tau_g, se_g, p_g, pct_g))

# Final clear numerical result: main estimate reiterated
cat("\n=== Final reported estimate ===\n")
tau <- main_fit$est$tau
se  <- main_fit$est$se
p   <- main_fit$est$p
pct <- 100 * (exp(tau) - 1)
cat(sprintf("Causal jump at 50%% (log points): %.4f (SE = %.4f), p = %.4f\n", tau, se, p))
cat(sprintf("Implied percent change in spending: %.2f%%\n", pct))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Passing the initiative (≥50%) should increase targeted policy spending relative to just-failing cases.
- Magnitude: A local jump around 0.10–0.25 log points, implying roughly a 10%–28% increase in spending at the cutoff. The exact estimate depends on bandwidth choice, but should be stable across reasonable specifications and pass density (no-manipulation) and placebo-cutoff checks.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — cutoff = 50% vote share; local linear regression with optimal bandwidth
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Passing the initiative causes a discrete jump in targeted spending
